deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: No evidence/reviewed-repository-inventory.json baseline was created to enable a two-way diff via tools/extract_repository_inventory.py, even though the current snapshot was regenerated.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Establishing THE reviewed baseline is inherently a project-owner/reviewer decision about what state is approved (the plan's own S0 origin story implies a human-reviewed checkpoint, not an AI-fabricated one), especially mid-stream with uncommitted work still in the working tree -- baselining now would compare future work against a not-yet-reviewed state, defeating the mechanism's purpose.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: tools/extract_repository_inventory.py can only report 'SNAPSHOT-DERIVED -- MUST RECOMPUTE' (no baseline supplied) rather than a real match/mismatch verdict, for this and any future stage, until the user (or a future session, at the user's direction) establishes one.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: No CI job builds the production profile through the real ESP-IDF container on every push/PR, even though this pass proves a full production build succeeds.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Adding a new CI job (container selection, secrets/timing implications, failure-mode design) deserves its own deliberate pass rather than being folded into a Kconfig/partition-layout verification pass.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: A future regression in the production profile or partition layout would not be caught automatically until someone re-runs this same manual verification.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Unchanged reasoning from the prior pass's evidence -- these are separate, distinct pieces of remaining work, not addressed by this pass's specific focus (the partition-table blocker).
